factual_summaries: OpenAI described Codex Remote as a way to start, steer, review, and organize engineering work from a mobile control surface while tasks continue on development machines.
Axios reported growing Codex use and emphasized that agents are moving from chat toward delegated work, with sampled Codex users submitting tasks estimated to represent substantial human work.
TechRadar framed AI coding systems as strategic infrastructure and argued the bottleneck is shifting from code generation speed to independent verification, governance, auditability, and continuity.
Augment Code published guidance that production AI agents can fail semantically behind healthy infrastructure signals and need trace-level telemetry, evaluation, and orchestration instrumentation.
The public awesome-harness-engineering list surfaced a June 2026 definition of an agent harness around an agent loop, tool interface, context management, and control mechanisms.

A June 2026 arXiv paper argues that coding-agent rules files, agent definitions, and IDE-specific markdown form an unmanaged control layer and proposes deterministic validation for configuration provenance, permissions, constraints, and tool scopes.
A June 2026 paper models coding-agent orchestration as cost-sensitive sequential testing, deciding when to gather evidence, refine, verify, or stop based on uncertainty and verifier cost.

TechRadar argued that secure enterprise agents should preserve existing human approval, permission, and audit workflows by operating through established interfaces rather than bypassing controls through backend access.
